chunks: Saad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Habib al-Kha'thami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would pray the night prayer in the month of Ramadan, then he would become junub, then he would deliberately delay the ritual bath until dawn rises.

It is not established in it that he deliberately delayed the bath without an excuse; it is permissible that he only delayed the bath due to an excuse, either for fetching the water or for warming it in the cold, or due to an incidental reason, because when one of these excuses occurs, delaying the bath is permissible and neither making up the prayer nor expiation is required.
And we have clarified previously what indicates this meaning, so there is no basis for repeating it.

And regarding the one who rinses his mouth and the one who inhales water, we have clarified their ruling: if it is for prayer, there is nothing upon him regarding what enters his throat from it; but if it is for other than prayer, and it enters his throat, then he must make up the prayer and expiation is required of him.
And this is also indicated by what he narrated.

key_terms.الْمُتَمَضْمِضُ: The one who rinses his mouth

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on delaying ghusl until dawn in Ramadan and does it require expiation?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between intentional neglect and valid excuses (*'udhr*) for delaying *ghusl* until Fajr, thereby avoiding the heavier penalty of *kaffarah*. It further clarifies that the requirement for expiation applies specifically when water is swallowed during non-prayer acts like rinsing or inhaling, whereas such acts performed for prayer do not incur penalty. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on contextualizing prophetic actions to derive precise legal rulings regarding ritual purity and fasting validity.
